title: Master 80% of Google Antigravity in 27 Minutes
summary: Beginner tutorial for Google Antigravity: editor vs agent manager, spec in markdown, multi-agent tasks, Firebase MCP, safety settings.

assertions.quote: It will perform much better if you plug it into a markdown file and let it use that

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: I prefer to always have the human in the loop approach. So, I have the chance to adjust it before it builds

verdicts.note: Plan-then-execute consistently reduces agent rework in practice and in vendor evals, especially on multi-file tasks.

assertions.quote: for any design-related tasks, I find that Gemini performs better

verdicts.note: Model strengths do differ by task in benchmarks and practice, but the specific pairing is personal preference and shifts each release.

assertions.quote: Use a disposable clone or a container for risky tasks

verdicts.note: Agents have deleted files and run destructive commands when unrestricted; vendors themselves recommend containers/VMs for skip-permissions modes.

assertions.quote: even if you've never tried anything like this before

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.
45% of sources stress accessibility for novices and non-programmers. That evidence is mostly grey literature and centered on prototypes.
